title: RAW UNREVIEWED: a repeated process consumes an explicitly referenced prior-stage result
summary: The same paid operation can act first on a written initial input and later on a written earlier result. Initial/medial occurrence is explained by event dependency, not new process glosses or automatic entry scope.

design.mechanism: Use fixed P(input)->result with paid preconditions. A later P may consume the earlier result only through an explicitly written, already-priced event/result reference and compatible input type. Preserve original input, result and separate operation episodes.
design.prediction: A whole chain must expose the first written input, each produced result and each reference authorizing reuse. Repeated P retains identical transition semantics; result state must meet its preconditions or an explicit paid restoration operation is required.
design.contrast: Explicit result-fed iteration versus independent repeated instructions acting on separately written inputs.
design.scope: No nearest-result fallback, invisible restoration, layer ownership census or missing-patient repair.

required_falsifier: Reject if a later P requires a result that was never produced/referenced, violates unchanged process preconditions, silently replaces an independent input, or changes P to permit repetition.
exact_changed_research_decision: Prefer result-fed repetition only when the complete paid graph predicts lawful input reuse; otherwise retain independent-event rival or leave binding unresolved.
